title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 29, 2026
summary: A sixth heat dome of the season pushed into Italy and the Balkans from 27 August, driving temperatures to 42-43°C across the Po Valley, Croatia, Hungary, Serbia and Bosnia and threatening to further delay the Danube's recovery. Romania's Cernavodă nuclear plant remained fully offline as authorities raced to complete a temporary guide dam on the Old Danube arm and continued releasing water from Olt River reservoirs, with flow still holding near a third of the historical average. The EU's cumulative 2026 burned area rose to 634,473 hectares as of 27 August, with the fire-danger map continuing to shift east. Aragón's Peñas de Riglos fire, which killed a UME soldier and forced over 1,000 evacuations, was confirmed stabilized at an 18,400-hectare perimeter after the region's largest-ever firefighting mobilization.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: Belgium's largest wildfire on record burned roughly 3,000 hectares in the High Fens and pushed smoke toward Germany, while a Spanish UME soldier was killed fighting Aragón's 16,600-hectare Peñas de Riglos fire, which also forced 1,045 evacuations. Greece evacuated 481 people by sea from a Halkidiki blaze, and a second Landes fire near Luglon burned 1,700 hectares before being contained. Romania restarted a 300 MW coal unit at Rovinari and unblocked the long-delayed Bala 2 project to secure future Danube cooling water, as both Cernavodă reactors remained offline. EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 burned area at 619,613 hectares, still below 2025's record pace, while a new Bloomberg tally put Europe-wide heat deaths above 25,000 since April.
